title: RePM: Reconfigurable Elastic Computing for Polynomial Multiplier with Hybrid NTT Algorithm
problem: Lattice-based cryptography requires efficient polynomial multiplication via Number Theoretic Transform (NTT), but current ASIC/FPGA designs suffer from high resource consumption, low efficiency, and inflexible designs under strict power constraints.
motivation: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards like ML-KEM require practical hardware implementations; efficient, flexible NTT accelerators enable deployment in power-constrained environments.
method: RePM uses conflict-free near-memory mapping to reduce data relocation overhead, elastic butterfly unit architecture eliminating pre-computing, and mixed radix-2/4 NTT algorithm removing pre/post-processing stages. Architecture applies to multiple PQC algorithms under strict power constraints.
key_novelty: Elastic computing array architecture for NTT butterfly units with hybrid radix-2/4 algorithms and conflict-free memory mapping.
contributions: 17× higher throughput under strict power constraints
limitations: Evaluation focused on ML-KEM; applicability to other PQC algorithms (NTRU, Dilithium) not quantified; power constraint assumptions specific.
primary_theme: Efficient NTT acceleration for post-quantum cryptography
